h1: The 6 Best Bed Frames with Storage of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bed Frames with Storage: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six storage bed frames, from hydraulic lift-ups to drawer beds and an 18 inch tall metal frame, with weight and budget advice.
summary: The Jocisland lift-up frame is our best overall, with 40 percent more storage than a standard bed. The EMODA metal frame is the cheap, tall-clearance pick, the Lifezone drawer bed suits those who want reachable drawers, and the HISOFT is the only King size here.
intro: Storage beds hide a trade-off that most listings bury: a lift-up frame gives you one huge cavity that you reach only by raising the whole mattress, while a drawer bed gives small, easy compartments. If you will open it weekly, the mechanism matters more than the stated volume.
We reviewed eight listings and ranked six on weight capacity, access style and clearance. Everything comes from the spec sheets, not from assembly in a workshop.

products.name: Jocisland Queen Linen Lift Up Storage Wingback
products.verdict: A 1,000 lb lift-up frame with a squeak-resistant mechanism.
products.description:
The Jocisland is a Queen hydraulic lift-up bed with a 1,000 lb capacity. The lift opens to 60 inches, the linen wingback headboard stands 52.1 inches, and the listing claims 40 percent more storage than a standard bed.

It ranks first because the capacity is among the highest here and the mechanism is labeled squeak-resistant. The Allewie below offers 800 lb for a similar bucket.

It suits bulky bedding and luggage. The caveat is the $200 to $500 price.
products.idealFor: Owners with bulky bedding to store.

products.name: Allewie Queen Lift Up Hydraulic Storage
products.verdict: Gas hydraulic lift, solid wood slats and a linen finish.
products.description:
The Allewie is a Queen frame with an 800 lb capacity, gas hydraulic lift, solid wood slats and a linen-upholstered wingback headboard with channel design.

It ranks second because the capacity trails the Jocisland's 1,000 lb, though it has a similar feature set.

Good for a classic look. The caveat is the lower weight rating.
products.idealFor: Buyers who like a classic upholstered look.

products.name: SHA CERLIN Queen Lift Up Wingback Storage
products.verdict: Hydraulic lift platform that needs no box spring.
products.description:
The SHA CERLIN is a Queen frame with an 800 lb capacity and hydraulic lift platform. It has solid wood slats with plastic buckles, a wingback headboard with horizontal channels, and needs no box spring.

It ranks third because it matches the Allewie on capacity and bucket but gives fewer extras.

Suits those who want a simple lift. The caveat is the plastic buckles on the slats.
products.idealFor: People replacing an old box-spring bed.

products.name: Lifezone Queen 4 Drawers + LED + Charging
products.verdict: Four sliding drawers and a tiered headboard with charging.
products.description:
The Lifezone is a Queen bed rated for 800 lb. It pairs four sliding drawers with a two-tier headboard and two AC outlets, plus USB and Type-C charging. Lighting is RGB and can be driven from an app or a remote, and eleven metal rods support the frame.

It ranks fourth because drawers give easier access than lifting a mattress, but total volume is smaller.

Best for everyday access. The caveat is that drawers need floor clearance to slide.
products.idealFor: Daily access to socks and clothing.
products.skipIf: You need to store bulky items.

products.name: EMODA Queen 18 Inch Tall Metal Storage
products.verdict: The tallest under-bed clearance here, at the lowest price.
products.description:
The EMODA is a metal Queen frame with 18 inches of under-bed clearance, a 1,200 lb capacity, nine reinforced legs and tool-free assembly in about 20 minutes. It has DIY headboard mounting holes.

It ranks fifth because it offers no built-in drawers, so you supply the bins, but it is the cheapest at $50 to $100.

Ideal for bins and boxes. The caveat is no headboard comes with it.

products.name: HISOFT King Hydraulic Lift + Metal Slats + Linen
products.verdict: King size lift-up with full metal slats and noise foam.
products.description:
The HISOFT is a King frame with a 1,000 lb capacity, a pair of gas lifts, slats made entirely of metal, foam padding at the joints against noise, and a tufted linen wingback headboard.

It ranks last only because King size suits fewer rooms, though it is the only one here at that size.

Choose it for a large bedroom. The caveat is its size.
products.idealFor: Large bedrooms needing King size storage.

whatMatters.detail: Lift-up frames raise the whole platform to reveal one big cavity, while drawers slide out in sections. Lift-ups hold bulkier items but need space above the bed. Check the listing for the mechanism name.
This is the maximum load the frame supports, such as 800 or 1,000 lb. It includes the mattress and sleepers. Look for the pounds figure in the specs.
Clearance is the gap between floor and slats, like the EMODA's 18 inches. It decides whether bins fit. Look for the inch figure.
Queen and King frames need different room space. Measure the room including walkways. Listings state the size in the title.
Squeaks come from slat joints and lifts. Foam strips or noise padding help. Look for terms like noise foam or squeak-resistant.

faq.q: Do these need a box spring?
faq.a: The SHA CERLIN says no box spring needed. Check each listing for others.
Ignoring lift clearance. A lift-up bed needs room above and beside it to open fully.

faq.q: Is lift-up worth it over drawers?
faq.a: For bulky items yes. For daily clothes, the Lifezone drawers are easier.
The EMODA lists about 20 minutes and no tools. Others vary, so check the listing.
Tighten bolts periodically. The HISOFT adds EVA foam at every joint.
Check the slat spacing and the weight rating against your mattress.

finalTake: The Jocisland is the best storage bed here for bulky items. Choose the Lifezone for drawers, the EMODA for budget, or the HISOFT for a King room. Decide on access style before looking at looks.
